name: misharu-contracts
what_this_is: The deployed Misharu escrow contracts, their compiled artifacts, the addresses they run at, and the evidence that the deployed code matches this source. The adjudication engine is not part of this release.
what_this_is_not: Not audited. Verified means the deployed bytecode matches this source; it does not mean this source is correct.
Not the engine. The judge, the console and the protocol implementation are not here.
Testnet only. No mainnet deployment exists.

how_to_check.evm: Compile with the compiler version in the Sourcify record and compare, or read the verified source at the sourcify URL in deployments/verification.json.
how_to_check.cardano: aiken build, then blake2b-224 over the compiled script from plutus.json. The result is the on-chain script hash, and needs no third party.
how_to_check.solana: cargo build-sbf and compare the program bytes against the deployed program id.
how_to_check.sui: sui move build and compare against the published package.

files.what: Escrow: funding, submission, provisional verdict, challenge window, finalize, timeout refund.
Funds judge evaluation separately, with a capped platform fee and a timelock on raising it.
Which keys may sign a verdict for a given judge.
Aiken validator, Plutus V3. FinalizeAccept / FinalizeReject / Expire / MutualCancel.
Build configuration, including the exact stdlib revision the artifact was compiled against.
Compiled blueprint: the script bytes and their hash. blake2b-224 of the script reproduces the on-chain hash.
The Preprod address the blueprint compiles to.
Native Rust program: create-and-fund, submit, record provisional, finalize, expire-and-refund.
Crate manifest, pinning the toolchain the deployed program was built with.
Move module, including the two-step mutual cancel.
Package manifest.
Every deployment: network, address, and when it was recorded.
Named addresses, so a reader can tell a deployer from a party.
Sourcify results per EVM contract, including the exact_match status and when it was checked.
Compact contract with selective disclosure: manifest hash, evidence root and verdict always public; the work, the amount and the parties independently shieldable.

The bounded variant: proves a shielded amount is within a PUBLIC cap. One bit reaches the ledger — a refused funding tells an observer the amount exceeded the cap, which is the only inference the design intends to permit.
Proves a committed measurement satisfies a public condition, publishing only the boolean. 81 and 99 both satisfy 'at least 80' and are indistinguishable on chain.
Many agreements in one long-lived contract, keyed by manifest hash. Every guarantee the single-escrow deployment got from being spent is an assertion here, so registry-sim.mjs attacks them directly.

m-of-n enforced on chain: m distinct registered finalizers must approve, each in their OWN transaction from their own machine. Nine slots, so 2-of-3, 4-of-6 and 5-of-9 all fit. A counter alone would let one holder approve twice and satisfy a 2-of-3 by themselves.
The compiler's own statement of what reaches the public ledger, what stays a private witness, and which circuits require a proof.
Noir: proves a committed measurement satisfies a public threshold. The commitment binding is load-bearing — without it the circuit proves a statement about a number nobody agreed to.

Noir: proves you know the CONTENT of an item in a committed evidence tree, without revealing which item or where. Takes the content and not the leaf, because a disclosure package hands its recipient the leaves of the items it withheld.
16 vectors both the Noir circuit and the TypeScript implementation answer to.
7 trees, 30 inclusion cases, odd sizes included — a promoted node contributes no sibling, and a naive implementation drops it and still produces a plausible root.
Generated UltraHonk verifier for the predicate circuit, live on Base Sepolia. Its five assembly blocks are annotated memory-safe to compile; that annotation is UNAUDITED.
Generated UltraHonk verifier for the membership circuit, live on Base Sepolia. Same unaudited memory-safe annotation.

Recovers Wormhole guardian signatures over a Pyth attestation and refuses anything short of quorum. Before this, 'the guardians signed it' was a claim our adapter made and signed; now a stranger can check the same bytes against a public node with nothing of ours involved.
The pinned Wormhole guardian set the verifier is deployed with. Pinned on purpose: a contract accepting whatever set index a VAA declared would accept a set nobody told it about.
The VAA verifier on Base Sepolia, with the command to check an attestation yourself.
Zero-dependency receipt verifier. Node or a browser, no install. Reports INCOMPLETE where a check could not run — a check that did not happen is never a pass.
How to run the verifier and what each result means.
The panel rules: what makes a quorum valid, and how votes are counted. Published so a tally can be recomputed from the votes without asking our server anything.
JCS canonical JSON and the domain-separated commitments everything is signed over.
Committed amounts: how a price is hidden from the panel, and how the two parties reproduce the digest.
The predicate, registry and multisig deployments on Midnight Preprod, with every transaction.
A 2-of-3 panel — two people and one AI agent — whose quorum was enforced on chain.
The predicate verifier on Base Sepolia, with the commands to check it without trusting this file.
The membership verifier on Base Sepolia, proven against a real case's published evidence root.
Every supported combination of decider, privacy, oracle and rail, with what each one costs and what is not built.
Apache 2.0.

non_evm.name: Cardano Preprod
non_evm.status: LIVE — all four redeemers executed on-chain, 12/12 edge cases rejected, and judgements settled end-to-end with the escrow datum bound to the bundle
non_evm.path: Aiken Plutus V3 validator, same lifecycle as JudgeEscrowV1: FinalizeAccept/FinalizeReject (finalizer-signed, after the challenge window, before recovery), Expire (unblockable refund by anyone), MutualCancel. Timing proved by the tx validity interval; payouts checked against datum credentials.
non_evm.grant: Pyth grant M3 vehicle — decision tracked in issue #2

expire.note: Recovery deadline passed; anyone may refund the buyer. Script address drained to 0.

finalize_accept.note: Finalizer-signed ACCEPT inside the window; provider paid.

settlements.edge_cases: deployments/cardano-edge-cases.json — 12/12 rejected by script evaluation, across all four redeemers

mutual_cancel.note: Buyer and provider are DIFFERENT keys and both signed; the agreement was unwound by consent and the buyer refunded. With one key playing both roles this redeemer cannot be tested — a single signature would satisfy both checks.

finalize_reject.note: Finalizer-signed REJECT inside the window; the buyer was refunded while the provider — a different key — received nothing. The mirror of finalize_accept, and the path that proves a verdict can move funds in either direction.

accept.note: Provider paid. The provider is a different key from the buyer, so the payout is a real transfer rather than change returning to the same wallet.

settled_judgements.binding: Each lock datum carries the bundle's manifest_hash and evidence_root. `pnpm cardano:verify-binding` reads the datum back from Koios and compares — the escrow and the judgement governing it are provably the same agreement, not two records filed together.

non_evm.name: Solana Devnet
non_evm.path: Native Rust program (no Anchor). Job account holds state and lamports; same invariants as JudgeEscrowV1 — settle at most once, provider-only submit, finalizer-only verdicts, committed challenge-window floor enforced on-chain, and ExpireAndRefund with no signature check so the recovery path can never be blocked.

non_evm.name: Sui Testnet
non_evm.status: LIVE — republished after fixing a confirmed authority bug; settles end-to-end
non_evm.path: Move package: shared Job object holding Balance<SUI>. Same invariants as JudgeEscrowV1 — settle at most once, only the provider submits, only the declared finalizer decides, committed challenge-window floor enforced on-chain, expire_and_refund callable by anyone after the recovery deadline.

history.reason: mutual_cancel authorised the buyer alone, letting a buyer reclaim the whole escrow after the provider delivered. Confirmed on testnet, then fixed. Do not use.

non_evm.name: Midnight Preprod (ZK)
non_evm.status: LIVE — fifteen cases settled on preprod with real ZK proofs, each on its own contract, and seven of those judgements were then settled cross-chain on Cardano preprod, Solana devnet and Base Sepolia. Two cases commit multi-item Merkle evidence roots, so a party can disclose part of the evidence to one recipient and have it verified against the chain. The work, the amount and the parties are witnesses to the circuits and reach no ledger.
non_evm.path: Same lifecycle as every other rail — open, fund, settle — with the work, the amount and the parties as WITNESSES rather than ledger state. The manifest hash, the evidence root, the verdict and the parties' disclosure choice are always public; a shielded verdict could only be acted on by whoever wrote it. A second variant adds a public cap and proves inside the circuit that the shielded amount is under it, so a payment can be shown to be within a mandate without being shown.

variants.proves: commitments only — a shielded amount is opaque rather than bounded
additionally: the shielded amount is at or under a cap committed before funding, proven in the circuit without revealing it
variants.evidence: the fund circuit's ZKIR grows 551 -> 791 bytes against the baseline, which is the constraint compiled in rather than written down

caveat: Shielding hides the evidence from the CHAIN, not from the JUDGE — a judge must read the work to decide it, so whoever operates that judge reads it too. Hiding it from them needs an attested enclave and is separate work.

ONE DEPLOYED CONTRACT HOLDS ONE ESCROW. `open` asserts the initial status, so a contract carries a single agreement for life and every case needs its own deployment. That is the design working — an escrow that could be reopened could be reused — but it does not amortise. A contract keyed by a map of manifest hashes is the obvious next version and is not built.

The dust wallet re-syncs ~1.43M indices (about 70 minutes) on every PROCESS start. FluentWalletBuilder exposes no serialize or restore, so the suite runs every case in one session; a process per case would be nine syncs.

`pnpm verify` does NOT accept these bundles. They settle in the circuits and carry no signed provisional envelope, so the offline signature verifier has nothing to check and records them as cannot_verify with that reason. They are backed by re-reading the ledger instead: `npx tsx contracts/midnight/deploy/read-ledger-check.mjs`.
non_evm.contracts_note: Reference deployments recorded for the registry. Each CASE deploys its own contract, because one contract holds one escrow — see the caveats.

verification.method: Sourcify recompiles the submitted source and compares the result to the bytecode on chain. An exact_match means the metadata hash agrees too, so it is the same build — not merely equivalent behaviour.
